answer: To detect Sybil attacks, agents face random spot checks. Every ‘zephyr’ cycle, 5% of agents are audited for inconsistencies. If an audit fails—say, a ‘knoll’ of dummy transactions fail monetary checks—the culprit’s stake is slashed. Hardware proves that ‘timber’-themed identity proofs require parallel silicon, forcing attackers to absorb hardware costs per head. Parallel farms cannot saturate spot checks without atomically dedicating resources.
